old_title: Football transfer deadline day: Manchester City move for Fernández, Villa sign Mbaye, and more - live
new_title: Transfer deadline day: Man City sign Fernández and Ndiaye, Mudryk and Tosin join Spurs - as it happened
old_text:
Thanks Will and hi all. Jay Boothroyd and Jamie O'Hara are currently arguing on SSN about whether Bruno Guimarães is one of the best midfielders in the world; it's compelling stuff, I can assure you.
Everton have registered interest in Lyon's Ashley Maitland-Niles amid uncertainty over getting the deal done for Kenny Tete. A £9m fee had been agreed with Fulham for the right back but with their move for a replacement in serious doubt - Andrei Ratiu of Rayo Vallecano - Everton are now exploring a move for the former Arsenal player. Maitland-Niles, 29, is in the final year of his contract with Lyon.
Aston Villa have sealed the £25m arrival of Taylor Harwood-Bellis from Southampton. The centre-back, who came through Manchester City's academy, is in effect Ezri Konsa's replacement. Harwood-Bellis watched on from the stands as Konsa made his Arsenal debut against Villa on Monday. Villa also held talks with Club Brugge's Joel Ordonez but were spooked by the Ecuador defender's metatarsal injury. That looks likely to be it for Villa, with Ibrahim Mbaye's £47m move from Paris Saint-Germain confirmed earlier.
Spurs are set to add Tosin Abarabioyo and Myhailo Mudryk before the deadline while they continue to trim fringe players with Kota Takai the latest out of the door. The Japan centre-half has gone to Sint-Truidense in Belgium on a season-long loan. Spurs have already announced the loan departures of Souza and Mikey Moore to Porto and FC Koln respectively.
The club's major out-goings to follow today are Kevin Danso to Sunderland on an initial loan followed by a mandatory £25m purchase and Pape Sarr to Juventus on an initial loan with a buy option. That deal is valued at around 30m euros. Spurs are expected to try to find a move for Dane Scarlett, who has only one year to run on his contract while Richarlison's future will continue to be monitored. He wants to leave. But is there a buyer for him?
Abarabioyo will replace Danso as a central defensive option for Roberto De Zerbi and cost around £7m from Chelsea. The London rivals have not done business since 2009 when Carlo Cudicini was allowed to go from Chelsea to Spurs on a free transfer. It is Mudryk's proposed move - a loan with an option to buy - that has the real shock factor.
The Ukrainian winger has not played since November 2024 because of a doping ban but he is free to play again after a resolution was reached between the Football Association and the World Anti-Doping Agency. De Zerbi has wanted a new player for the left wing and missed out on Iliman Ndiaye, who is going from Everton to Manchester City in a deal worth up to £65m, and Cody Gakpo, who is staying at Liverpool. De Zerbi worked with Mudryk at Shakhtar Donetsk and believes he can revive his career.
Abarabioyo and Mudryk stand to be the ninth and tenth new signings of the summer for Spurs. The Abarabioyo deal would take their spending to £311.5m.
Arsenal have confirmed the departure of Fabio Vieira to Hamburg on a permanent basis for around £8.7m. The Portuguese midfielder spent last season on loan at the German club. We are still waiting for confirmation of Gabriel Martinelli's move to Al Hilal and that Barcelona have completed the signing of Gabriel Jesus. But will the champions make a move for another attacker after the news that Malick Fofana - who was offered to Arsenal - is off to Sunderland instead?
Tony Hughes writes: "I'm an old man with young adult children. I cannot help feeling a little sad for these young men (and women) whose fate is decided by someone else, and who may end up leaving their club - their home - today and never returning.
"On top of that you're suddenly inserted into another country, with perhaps an unfamiliar language and faces.
"I get they're well paid for this for the most part however being a young adult is tough, and - Harvey Elliot is a good example - the churn in your professional life must be quite taxing."
A bit more from Jamie Jackson on matters Manchester-related.
Left-back Harry Amass is on Wolves's list - so may make a move as, for now, Burnley's interest seems to have flatlined. Also might City's final fee for Enzo Fernandez break the £125m British record fee? This was paid for Alexander Isak by Liverpool to Newcastle.
There is not the same intensity to club rivalries between women's teams as there is between their men's counterparts, but as the game grows that is changing. Increasingly, there is animosity from fans if a player leaves for a rival side.
Victoria Pelova's move from Arsenal to Tottenham firmly bucks the trend, though. Despite arguably having her best years ahead of her, the 27-year-old departed with a lot of well-wishes and love.
Another Chelsea outgoing could be Dario Essugo to Strasbourg on loan. But that would see Chelsea use up their last international loan slot. If that happens it would end any chance of Jamie Gittens going to Roma on loan.
Roland Marshall emails: "With a lot of talk about Joshua Zirkee's possible move paving the way for an incoming left-back, or the lack of it meaning one is not coming in, could the club do worse than actually invest some confidence in Harry Amass as an understudy to Luke Shaw? And similarly, Chido Obi as an understudy to Sesko (and possibly Zirkzee)? It's not as if the club don't have a good record with bringing youth through into the first team (Mainoo and Rashford for current examples in the team and I won't patronize you with detailing past illustrations of this fact).
"Or now with Ineos partially at the reins, is the academy now seen as a cash cow to make money from sales to other PL or EFL clubs (though with many former United academy players having plied their trade to varying levels of success across the divisions since 'You can't win anything with kids', there is the argument that thus it ever was, though I can't seem to remember them wanting to make as much filthy lucre from it in the past)."
The latest on Enzo Fernández it is the understood Manchester City have made offer worth more than £120m - the valuation Chelsea gave when setting the original 14 August deadline - which obviously passed with no offer. The No 8 is more than keen to move so all depends on Chelsea with regards whether can they get a replacement or just accept the price right ...
Aston Villa have completed the £47m signing of Ibrahim Mbaye from Paris Saint-Germain. It is thought Mbaye, who attended Monday's defeat at home to Arsenal, has signed a five-year contract with the option of a further 12 months. The 18-year-old Senegal forward has been tracked by Villa since breaking in at PSG, for whom he made his debut aged 16. Liverpool were among the clubs to show interest in the teenager earlier this window. Mbaye's arrival represents a major coup for Villa and offers Unai Emery something he has wanted all summer: a pacy wide player who can stretch defences. Talking of defenders, the £25m signing of Taylor Harwood-Bellis from Southampton will also be rubber-stamped shortly.
Sunderland agree deal to sign Arsenal target Fofana
Louise Taylor
Sunderland seem to have won the race to sign Malick Fofana from Lyon. The 21-year-old winger had been on Arsenal's summer shopping list but he is now flying to the north east to complete his medical.
Fofana is expected to sign a five year deal at the Stadium of Light. The transfer is set to cost an initial £25m, potentially rising to £31m.
Arsenal had wanted to recruit Fofana on loan with an option to buy next summer.
Doug Fenner gets in touch to say: "I realise the world, or the universe, revolves around the Premier League, but who on Earth thought it was a good idea to have transfer deadline day on a day where there is almost a full slate of EFL fixtures (or vice versa)?
"L1 and L2 clubs in particular aren't overburdened with support staff and so are those that are available supposed to be in two places at once, getting points and players at the same time?
"Fans will be scouring the team sheets before kick-off tonight to see which if their favourites are strangely missing from line-ups, perhaps for ever."
It does feel like a naive decision but at least everyone has had plenty of time to plan.
Billy Munday is on La Liga duty today, with plenty of transfer-related notions.
If Raphinha has any misgivings about playing as a makeshift No 9 for Barcelona, he is doing a good job of hiding it. Julián Álvarez would have been proud of the Brazilian's two neat finishes that inspired the Spanish champions to a 5-2 victory against Rayo Vallecano on Monday night, 24 hours before the transfer deadline. Lamine Yamal scored two wonderful goals of his own in a performance that reassured everyone he is back to his best. Add Anthony Gordon to the mix - impressive again in his link-up play - and you have a fluid, fearsome front three.
Yet after the departures of Ferran Torres, Robert Lewandowski and Marcus Rashford this summer, there is no doubt Barcelona not only still want a centre-forward but require one - at least one. Hansi Flick was very happy to see Gabriel Jesus, an £8.6m arrival from Arsenal, in the stands. "He's a top striker," the coach said. But Atlético Madrid's Álvarez is the ultimate prize.
Kevin Wilson writes: "Crazy amounts of money spent by the three promoted clubs. They've outspent most of the other established clubs outside of the Champions League clubs (and Spurs!) A huge gamble, least of all as most of the signed players have no experience of English football. I suppose they will sell or loan them out if the worst happens."
I think it is the nature of the modern game, namely because the difference between the Championship and Premier League is growing. Without spending, there is zero chance of staying up.
I believe Monaco are not keen to sell Camara at all this summer, especially after offloading Aladji Bamba to Newcastle. Folarin Balogun's move to Everton will also bring in plenty of cash, so if Chelsea really do want Camara, then it will cost them more than €45m, I suspect.
Chelsea have made a €45m bid for Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara, one of the potential replacements for Enzo Fernandez. The Fernandez to City deal remains "up in the air", with talks ongoing. Sources say there's no chance Chelsea get Alex Scott out of Bournemouth today.
Chelsea are also pushing for Manu Kone but Gasperini wants to keep the France midfielder at Roma.
Defender Zach Abbott is set to depart boyhood club Nottingham Forest to join Southampton on an initial loan deal, which could become permanent in the summer.
Hull have added another signing in the form of Ilyas Ansah from Union Berlin. The forward has cost the Tigers £21m and signed a five-year deal with the club.
"I'm very excited," Ansah said. "It's a dream come true for me to play in the Premier League, and for such a big club - it's really an honour for me. I have heard a lot about the club, the players and the team, and I'm excited to play with the boys and to get to know them. It was an honour and a dream playing in the Bundesliga. Now, I have another dream to play in the Premier League, and I'm going to work hard for it."
Ipswich are on course to complete the signing of Burnley striker Zian Flemming, who is Suffolk-bound this morning to complete his medical and other formalities.
The arrival of Flemming, who scored 11 top-flight goals for the doomed Clarets last season, ends Gary O'Neil's search for a senior centre-forward and comes after loan target Tammy Abraham chose to stay at Aston Villa.
As things stand that is the only business that will be done at Portman Road this deadline day and the fee, thought to be around £17m, will push the promoted side's summer spend towards £200m.
In what will be a very busy day for the Tigers, they are aiming to sign Brooke-Norton Cuffy from Genoa, Tim Iroegbunam from Everton and Robinio Vaz from Roma.
Andy Flintoff emails: "Your current picture at the top of the feed (@ 9.55am) obviously shows that Enzo Fernandez was a dab hand at the intra-squad Give Us A Clue competition and would be a big loss if he left Chelsea."
Leeds are closing in on a sixth summer signing with the left-back Melvin Bard set to swap Nice for West Yorkshire in a one-year deal featuring an option to buy next summer.
Meanwhile Wilfried Gnonto's hopes of starting a new life in Florence with Fiorentina look contingent on Daniel Farke being able to sign a replacement wide attacker by the end of today.
Crystal Palace are adamant that Ismaila Sarr will not be leaving in this window after rejecting an offer from Liverpool for the Senegal forward. With Cody Gakpo now expected to stay at Anfield, it remains to be seen whether they or anyone else make another approach for Sarr, who is understood to have been unsettled by the interest and has deleted all references to Palace from his social media accounts.
The Conference League winners are no strangers to a frenetic final day of the window and there could be plenty of movement again with teenage defender Honest Akanor set to sign on loan from Atalanta and Palace also eyeing up a new central midfielder. Celtic have made an approach to sign Justin Devenny on loan, while Borna Sosa, David Ozoh, Jesurun Rak-Sakyi and Romain Esse are other potential departures.
No further incomings are expected at Liverpool following the £123m arrival of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain on Monday. There could be several outgoings, but none from Andoni Iraola's first team plans after bids for Cody Gakpo and Trey Nyoni were rejected from Manchester City and Nottingham Forest, respectively. Anfield departures are likely to all be loans too - Harvey Elliott to Valencia, with no obligation to buy, is the main one while the fit-again Jayden Danns has offers from several Championship clubs.
new_text:
Some last-gasp breaking news, and it's not good for Everton fans - the move for Monaco forward Folarin Balogun is off (unless, of course, a certain satsuma-hued powerbroker decides to step in). Andy Hunter has more ...
Time to call it a night. Here are the day's big stories - and keep following our interactive guide for every last deal before we take our ball home until 1 January.
Late moves aplenty still going through, with Zian Flemming joining Ipswich for £20m, and Hull City making their sixth deadline-day signing in the shape of Greek midfielder Christos Mouzakitis. Follow along with our transfer interactive ...
More on Enzo Fernández's arrival at the Etihad, via an official statement.
Manchester City have completed the signing of Enzo Fernández from Chelsea on a five-year contract. The Argentina international's deal means he will remain at the Etihad Stadium until the summer of 2031.
Fernández says he could not be happier to have joined City at this stage of his career. "Manchester City are the most successful club in England in recent times. Every player wants to be part of a club like this because everyone knows how well-run City are.
"I could not be happier to be here, and I am ready for the challenge of helping City continue winning trophies. This is a club built for success," Fernández added. "If you look across the squad, City have quality in every area. I want to learn from my new teammates and become a better player.
"I pride myself on continually improving my game. Anyone who's worked with me will know how hard I train every single day and how much I put into matches. I give absolutely everything and I can promise Manchester City that will continue now I'm here.
City's director of football, Hugo Viana, added: "At Manchester City, we are always looking to bring in world-class players and Enzo fits the bill. He is a complete midfielder: technically gifted, hardworking, tenacious and a goalscorer.
"He is adept at playing different styles of football. He is comfortable playing a possession-based game, and he can play on the counter effectively, too. We are delighted to bring him here and feel very strongly he will improve our team."
It's the biggest transfer fee of the window, and now it's official: Manchester City have signed Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernández for a club-record £125m.
You wait 17 years for a Spurs-Chelsea transfer deal, and two come along in one evening. After agreeing a loan move for Mykhailo Mudryk earlier, Tottenham have signed Chelsea centre-back Tosin Adarabioyo for around £7m.
According to Sky Sports, there are at least six deal sheets in the Premier League's inbox, with three of those coming from Selhurst Park, as Ed Aarons reports below. There's also Folarin Balogun's Everton move and Malick Fofana on his way to Sunderland; the other deal sheet comes from Leeds, for Eintracht Frankfurt winger Jean-Matteo Bahoya.
Chelsea's move for Lamine Camara collapsed after Everton's move for Monaco's Folarin Balogun was revived. Balogun's move looked in doubt after complications with his medical, meaning Monaco needed funds from elsewhere, leaving Chelsea to swoop for Camara as a replacement for Enzo Fernández before his move to Manchester City.
However Everton have persisted and renegotiating their fee for Balogun led to Monaco pulling out of the Camara deal. Chelsea are livid, with sources calling Monaco's behaviour deeply unprofessional. Chelsea had a written agreement with the Ligue 1 side. It's important to add this development won't scupper the Fernández deal to City.
Crystal Palace have submitted deal sheets for Ben Chilwell, Dario Osario and Quinten Timber after dramatically missing out Malick Fofana earlier. Pierre Sage wanted to bring in more reinforcements ahead of a season that will see Palace play in the Europa League. Chilwell will replace Borna Sosa as cover for Tyrick Mitchell after the Croatia defender joined Köln on loan.
Palace turned to Osario - the Chile winger who plays for Midtjylland in Denmark - after Fofana opted to join Sunderland. They have also revived a move for Netherlands midfielder Timber (the twin brother of Arsenal's Jurriën) from Marseille after failing to agree a fee for Mainz's Kaishu Sano earlier in the day.
Lamine Camara's move to Chelsea is OFF, Jacob Steinberg confirms. It looked like the Monaco midfielder was set to complete a £47m move, but that won't be happening. Enzo Fernández's move to Manchester City is not affected by the Camara deal.
Here's the first mention of a deal sheet, in relation to Everton and their pursuit of Folarin Balogun, who could probably live without any more admin drama.
"Everton have submitted a deal sheet to complete the Balogun deal after trying to renegotiate the structure of the fee with Monaco. Maitland-Niles deal expected to go through," reports Andy Hunter.
Enzo Fernandez has penned a -long - heartfelt message to Chelsea fans after his £125m move to Man City.
Want to read it?
Dear Chelsea.
I want you to know that these have not been easy days for me. Writing this is not easy either. The truth is, I haven't been in a good place.
Three years ago, Cobham and Stamford Bridge became home for me and my family. I grew attached to the people, to the shirt, and to the badge of this incredible club.
Believe me when I say that, from the moment I arrived, I became obsessed with winning and with bringing this club every trophy that its history deserves. We suffered, we cried, I got angry many times, but we also celebrated titles and unforgettable victories. Together, through the good times and the difficult ones.
I live football the same way I live my life: with passion and with all my heart. That is why I want you to know that I understand you. I truly understand you, from the bottom of my heart.
But life is about making decisions, and right now I find myself having to make one of those difficult decisions. I've said it before, but I want to say it again: I have grown incredibly fond of this club. Chelsea will always have a place in my thoughts and, above all, in my heart.
But I also understand how football works. I know how passionate you are, because I am the same. And if I were in your position, I would probably be thinking the same way.
I want to thank every single one of you: the staff, the coaching team, the medical team, the physios, and everyone who works at Cobham and throughout this great institution.
To all my teammates over these years, thank you from the bottom of my heart for sharing so many moments with me. I was truly happy here, and I wish you nothing but the very best for the future.
Thank you for all the love and support you have given me and my family throughout these years. I will never forget it.
This group will give you many more reasons to be happy, and I will be happy for you too. Never doubt that.
You will always be in my heart, Blues. I will always wish you, always, nothing but the very best.
Drew is copping quite a lot of heat from fellow Arsenal fans behind the scenes.
I can't share them all but let's just say he doesn't speak for all Gooners.
And as Rory Hoare points out, things could be worse than winning the league:
All my thoughts are with you Drew. As a spurs fan I cannot imagine the pain of winning the league, selling a couple of players and still looking like you'll win the league again. You poor lamb.
Understand Everton's offer for Joshua Zirkzee was in the region of £10m for the loan of the Manchester United forward and to cover his wages for the season - and Utd felt this was too low.
Drew Lundgren [great name by the way] is back for some more Arsenal ranting:
I dont think you can call Arsenal favorites with their turgid attack (turgid for YEARS now), and their front office spiraling out of control, ready to close the window with 2 fewer attackers than last year. They are 1 injury away Arteta dressing as back up striker.
Will there a be a deal secured that future generations look back on with awe? Will you, our dear reader, tell your grandkids that you were here, on our blog, to read all about it?
"Am told Joshua Zirkzee's proposed loan to Everton from Manchester United fell down because it was too late for United to source a replacement; United, it is understood, believe the Dutch forward can still contribute."
A couple of disgruntled Arsenal fans have written in.
Drew Lundgren:
Arsenal deadline day appears to be a failure. There is no imaginable reason to let Martinelli go with no replacement. The fans at the Emirates really need to get on the manager and Berta next time out. Chants, boos, they really need to let them know. It is a completely pathetic showing. Berta out.
Gary Stover:
Stan Knoenke not only owns Arsenal FC and the Los Angeles Rams, and is now buying the Los Angeles Angels MLB team, and through his wife, a descendant of Sam Walton (Walmart), they own the Denver Nuggets NBA franchise, the MLS Colorado Rapids, the NHL Colorado Avalanche.... Kroenke spearheaded the attempt to establish the European Super League. All of this doesn't make him a bad guy. He's simply using his money to buy and make money through ownership of sports franchises. He's not alone. In this environment who's to say how much an individual player is worth? or a team? If you have enough money to own a sports franchise, you have enough money to hire attorneys, who'll find a way around the "rules." One thing is certain--Man City is not worried about being in violation of anything anytime.
One signing Everton have got over the line is Jack Grealish, who has returned to the Hill Dickinson Stadium on another season loan from Manchester City.
The 30-year-old was enjoying a productive spell on loan last season before suffering a fractured foot that ended his campaign in February.
Grealish, who will be out of contract at City when this latest deal ends next summer, could make his second Everton 'debut' against Manchester United on Sunday.
He said: "I'm so happy. I think I'm at my best at everything in life, not just football, when I feel loved. That's what the manager has given me, what my teammates have given me and especially what the fans have given me. Every time I see an Everton fan, it's just pure love.
"It means a lot to me and hopefully I've made a few Everton fans happy. I had a perfect time here for the first six months, then I stayed around after I got injured. I've been watching all the Everton games in pre-season and since the season started. Now I feel ready to go."
Phew. What a hectic couple of minutes. Jamie, Ed, Jacob and David are motoring! Well done lads!
In the last few minutes we've had Tottenham land Mudryk on a loan deal from Chelsea, Everton failed to secure Zirkzee from Man United and Chelsea are waiting on Camara's medical.
Tottenham have announced the loan signing of Mischa Mudryk from Chelsea. They have a £75m option to buy the Ukraine winger. I hope it works out for Mudryk.
Just to add in the medical for Camara is already done. So we're just waiting for confirmation.
A crazy situation as Chelsea had bids rejected for him - then the breakdown of Everton's move for Folarin Balogun left Monaco needing another source of funds
Spurs pivoted to Ukraine international Mudryk on Monday after a dramatic finale to a remarkable summer transfer window for the north London club.
After no progress in a pursuit for Liverpool's Cody Gakpo, Tottenham reached an agreement in principle with Everton for Iliman Ndiaye on Sunday before Manchester City, having also missed out on Gakpo, hijacked the deal, forcing De Zerbi to turn to Mudryk.
Mudryk returned from a 20-month suspension last month and worked with De Zerbi at Shakhtar Donetsk before a transfer to Chelsea in 2023.
It has been a difficult time for the 25-year-old after he was banned in 2024 by the Football Association due to an "adverse finding" for meldonium. However, Mudryk will aim to rediscover his best form under De Zerbi on a season-long loan that includes a £75m option to buy.
Speaking during Tottenham's pre-season tour of Australia when Mudryk's ban ended, De Zerbi said: "He's my son. I'm very happy. He deserves to play. He's a cool guy, a top player. Hopefully he can show what he suffered in the last two years in this next season. Press Association.
Tim Iroegbunam has left Everton to join Hull City. The fee for the 23-year-old is undisclosed but is believed to be worth £15m plus £7m in add-ons, with Aston Villa receiving a sell-on sum as part of the deal that took the midfielder to Merseyside in 2024.
Getting word that Sunderland have won the mad race for Malik Fofana's signature.
The Black Cats had the deal wrapped up this morning - worth a reported £25.7m - but a faulty plane and some chutzpah from Crystal Palace, who tried to hijack the move, added some drama to the narrative.
Crystal Palace are set to sign Ben Chilwell for an undisclosed fee from Strasbourg as they continue to work right up until the deadline.
The former England defender spent the second half of last season at Selhurst Park on loan and is now on his way back to London, where he spent five years with Chelsea.
Palace are still trying to do deals for midfielder Quinten Timber from Marseille and a loan for Chile forward Darío Osorio from Danish side Midtjylland after apparently accepting defeat to Sunderland in their attempts to sign Malick Fofana from Lyon.
Everton have not pulled the plug on a deal for Folarin Balogun yet, despite problems with the US international's medical and making a loan move for Manchester United's Joshua Zirkzee. Still a chance the Balogun deal goes through.
Here's more on United's late effort to secure a leftback:
Am told Rayan Aït-Nouri was offered to Manchester United by his camp a few days ago - the club contacted City this afternoon and were told only a loan with obligation to buy was possible, which United baulked at.
Chelsea have agreed a £47m deal to sign Lamine Camara from Monaco.
The 22-year-old from Senegal joined Monaco from Metz in 2024 and has quickly established himself as one of Ligue 1's most dynamic midfielders.
Comfortable as a No 6 or No 8, he brings energy, ball-winning and progressive passing, while possessing a fierce shot and a reputation for dangerous set-pieces.
Evening Niall. The transfer window doesn't close slam shut until Thursday in Scotland, so still plenty time for rumours and actual deals up here. With Vicko Sevelj having left Tannadice for Azerbaijan outfit Neftci Baku, Dundee United have moved to secure Lyall Cameron on loan from Rangers and are looking at Josh Campbell of Hibs too. Celtic have taken Parma midfielder Oliver Sorenson on loan, and Portland Timbers striker Kevin Kelsy appears set to sign for Rangers. On Thursday, expect Lionel Messi and Cristiano Ronaldo to be spotted in Glasgow...
Manchester City have completed the signing of Iliman Nidaye for a fee that could rise to £65m. The Senegal international had three years remaining on his Everton contract and had scored 17 goals in 74 appearances for the club.
David Moyes said just over a week ago that it would take "an absolutely outrageous bid" for Everton to sell their prized asset yet the club's hierarchy, conscious of squad ratio cost pressures, have let him go for less than what City sold Savinho for.
With Beto gone and doubts emerging over Folarin Balogun's medical results, Ndiaye's exit could leave Everton in a very precarious position.
Manchester City have confirmed the signing of Iliman Ndiaye from Everton for £60m plus £5m, the 26-year-old signing a five-year contract.
The wide forward said: "City are one of the best clubs in the world and I've seen them win everything as I've grown up. To be able to write my own chapter in a story that special is the chance of a lifetime and I'm determined to grab it with both hands. It's not always been easy in my career, but I always had the belief that I could play for a team challenging for the biggest prizes and now I'm here. It feels so good. I love to play with the ball on the floor in an attacking team that wants to score as many goals as possible. That's why I know this is the perfect fit."
Ndiaye was loaned from Sheffield United, his first club, to Hyde United for the second half of the 2019-20 season and has also played for Marseille.
Thanks Niall. Phew, things are hotting up. Especially in the two-club race to sign Malik Fofana.
As Louise Taylor says:
Sunderland's owner, Kyril Louis-Dreyfus has flown to Lyon to try to persuade Malick Fofana to join Lyon rather than Crystal Palace and there is a sense Sunderland have won the race for his signature after the winger underwent a medical in France commissioned by both the north east club and Crystal Palace.
Sunderland, meanwhile, are hoping to sign a second winger in Benfica's Dodi Lukebakio before the deadline.
A big deal is now officially done: Manchester City have signed Everton forward Iliman Ndiaye in a transfer worth a reported £65m in total - £60m up front and £5m in add-ons.
"Manchester City is delighted to announce the signing of Iliman Ndiaye from Everton," an official statement said. "The 26-year-old forward has signed a five-year contract, keeping him at the Etihad Stadium until the summer of 2031."
Manchester United made a late enquiry to Manchester City for their left-back Rayan Aït-Nouri, but the 25-year-old will not be leaving. This seems a little late, and a scattergun approach from United.
"Why does Malick Fofana need to come to England at all tonight?" asks Iain Chambers. "Can't he just sign a contract of whichever club he eventually chooses, pop home for a kip, and make an early morning start on packing up his PlayStation & some autumn clothing choices?"
Yes, it's one of those old-fashioned curiosities of the transfer deadline that players must be whisked off to sign the paperwork in an empty stadium, when the whole thing could have been a Zoom call.
More on Malick Fofana's plane dilemma - Ed Aarons reports that "Palace manager Pierre Sage has also spoken to the 21-year-old on the phone again this evening, having made contact earlier on today. The pair previously worked together at Lyon." Presumably, Sage talked up Croydon's excellent transport links with Gatwick and central London.
Any Arsenal fans awaiting transfer updates: how about an entire baseball team? Stan Kroenke, owner of the Premier League champions and the NFL's LA Rams, is poised to buy the MLB's Los Angeles Angels, who are based in Anaheim.
There's a striker merry-go-round on the continent; with Nick Woltemade joining Juve on loan, Jonathan David has left Turin for Madrid, signing for Atlético on an initial loan. Júlian Alvarez, meanwhile, is still an Atleti player with the clock running down.
